overview.title: Deep Space Phenomena: The Universe's Most Extreme Events
overview.description: From gamma-ray bursts to gravitational waves, the cosmos' most powerful and mysterious events

gammaRayBursts.name: Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs)
gammaRayBursts.description: Most energetic explosions in universe since Big Bang
gammaRayBursts.energy: Releases more energy in seconds than Sun will in entire lifetime

causes.longGRB: Collapse of massive stars into black holes (hypernovae)
causes.shortGRB: Merger of neutron stars or neutron star + black hole

gammaRayBursts.detection: Can be seen from billions of light-years away
gammaRayBursts.danger: If one occurred within 6,000 light-years pointing at Earth, could cause mass extinction
gammaRayBursts.frequency: About once per day somewhere in observable universe
gammaRayBursts.famous: GRB 080916C - most luminous event ever recorded

fastRadioBursts.name: Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs)
fastRadioBursts.description: Mysterious millisecond radio pulses from deep space
fastRadioBursts.energy: Release as much energy as Sun does in days
theories: Alien technology (unlikely but not ruled out)
fastRadioBursts.repeating: Some repeat, others are one-time events
fastRadioBursts.breakthrough: FRB 200428 from magnetar in Milky Way confirmed magnetars as source

gravitationalWaves.name: Gravitational Waves
gravitationalWaves.description: Ripples in spacetime fabric predicted by Einstein

gw150914.source: Two black holes (29 and 36 solar masses) merging
gw150914.energy: 3 solar masses converted to gravitational wave energy

gw170817.significance: Observed in gravitational waves AND electromagnetic spectrum
gw170817.kilonova: Created heavy elements like gold and platinum

gravitationalWaves.future: LISA space-based detector (2030s) will detect supermassive black hole mergers

quasars.name: Quasars (Quasi-Stellar Objects)
quasars.description: Most luminous objects in universe - supermassive black holes feeding
quasars.luminosity: Can outshine entire galaxies of 100 billion stars
quasars.mechanism: Matter heating to millions of degrees as it falls into supermassive black hole
quasars.jets: Launch relativistic jets thousands of light-years long
quasars.farthest: ULAS J1342+0928 - 13.1 billion light-years, seen 690 million years after Big Bang

magnetars.name: Magnetars
magnetars.description: Neutron stars with strongest magnetic fields in universe
magnetars.danger: Could erase credit cards from 160,000 km away
magnetars.rotation: Spin as fast as 10 times per second
magnetars.formation: From supernovae of very massive stars

hypernovae.name: Hypernovae
hypernovae.description: Supernova explosion 5-50x more energetic than normal supernovae
hypernovae.cause: Collapse of extremely massive stars (>30 solar masses)
hypernovae.blackHole: Creates black hole or neutron star
hypernovae.grb: Often associated with long gamma-ray bursts
hypernovae.jets: Launch relativistic jets at near light-speed

pulsars.name: Pulsars
pulsars.description: Rapidly spinning neutron stars emitting beams of radiation
pulsars.lighthouse: Beam sweeps past Earth like cosmic lighthouse
pulsars.firstThought: Briefly considered alien signals ('LGM-1' = Little Green Men)
pulsars.millisecond: Millisecond pulsars spin hundreds of times per second
pulsars.binary: Some in binary systems being 'spun up' by companion

voids.name: Cosmic Voids
voids.description: Vast empty regions of space between galaxy filaments
voids.boötes: Boötes Void - 330 million light-years diameter, nearly empty

greatWall.name: Galaxy Walls and Filaments
greatWall.herculesCorona: Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall - 10 billion light-years, largest structure known

blazar.name: Blazars
blazar.description: Quasars with jets pointing directly at Earth
blazar.speed: Jets moving at 99.9% speed of light
blazar.neutrinos: TXS 0506+056 first source of high-energy neutrinos
blazar.observation: Appear as single point but galaxy-scale engine
blazar.danger: If nearby, jets could sterilize planets

tidal Disruption.name: Tidal Disruption Events
tidal Disruption.description: Star torn apart by supermassive black hole's gravity
tidal Disruption.process: Star stretched into stream of gas ('spaghettification')
tidal Disruption.flare: Creates bright flare visible across universe
tidal Disruption.science: Reveals black holes in galaxies we didn't know had them

collision.name: Galaxy Collisions
collision.description: Galaxies crash into each other over millions of years
collision.outcome: Trigger star formation, create new galaxy morphology
collision.milkyWay: Andromeda will collide with Milky Way in 4.5 billion years
collision.stars: Individual stars rarely collide due to vast distances

rogue Stars.name: Hypervelocity Stars
rogue Stars.description: Stars traveling fast enough to escape galaxy

roguePlanets.name: Rogue Planets (Free-Floating Planets)
roguePlanets.formation: Ejected from planetary systems or formed independently
roguePlanets.microlensing: Detected when pass in front of background star
roguePlanets.possibility: Could have subsurface oceans heated by radioactive decay

primordialBlackHoles.name: Primordial Black Holes
primordialBlackHoles.description: Hypothetical black holes formed in early universe
primordialBlackHoles.formation: From density fluctuations in first second after Big Bang
primordialBlackHoles.size: Could range from tiny to thousands of solar masses
primordialBlackHoles.planet Nine: Could Planet Nine be a primordial black hole?
primordialBlackHoles.hawking: Small ones would have evaporated by now via Hawking radiation

cosmicStrings.name: Cosmic Strings
cosmicStrings.origin: Formed during early universe phase transitions

vakaryonStars.name: Dark Stars (Hypothetical)
vakaryonStars.description: Theoretical stars powered by dark matter
vakaryonStars.size: Could be thousands of times larger than Sun
vakaryonStars.power: Dark matter annihilation instead of fusion
vakaryonStars.observation: JWST might see them as massive early stars
